title: IELTS guides and strategy — the Bloom blog
meta_description: Long-form guides from former examiners on writing structure, speaking fluency, reading timing and the band descriptors that decide your score.

props.heading: Written by the people who mark the papers.
props.lead: Strategy, format updates and requirement news. No listicles, no motivational filler — every post exists because a student asked the question in a lesson.

posts.title: Band 6.5 to 7.0: the four things that actually move the needle
posts.author: Dr. Elena Marchetti
posts.excerpt: Half a band is roughly a hundred focused hours — but only if those hours target the right four things. Here is what separates a 6.5 script from a 7.0 one, criterion by criterion.

posts.title: True / False / Not Given: a three-question procedure that removes the guesswork
posts.author: James Okonkwo
posts.excerpt: The most-failed question type in IELTS Reading, reduced to three questions you ask in order. Plus the qualifier words that turn a TRUE into a FALSE.

posts.title: Why your Part 2 answer runs out at 70 seconds — and four ways to fix it
posts.author: Michael Chen
posts.excerpt: Almost every candidate who fails Part 2 fails it the same way: they say everything they planned in seventy seconds and then stop. Four extension techniques that hold two minutes.

posts.title: Articles for Hindi, Urdu and Bengali speakers: the decision tree
posts.author: Anjali Prasad
posts.excerpt: If your first language has no article system, a/an/the is probably costing you more marks than anything else in your writing. Three questions, asked in order, fix most of it.

posts.title: UK university IELTS requirements 2027: what changed
posts.author: Paulo Mendes
posts.excerpt: Several Russell Group departments have raised their per-skill minimums for 2027 entry. A department-by-department summary, and what it means if you are sitting this autumn.

posts.title: OET or IELTS for GMC registration? An honest comparison
posts.author: Dr. Rana Yusuf
posts.excerpt: Both are accepted. One is dramatically easier if you already work in a clinical setting. The difference in what each exam asks you to do, and how to choose.

posts.title: Listening Part 1: the six formats that cost candidates ten marks
posts.author: Dr. Sarah Whitfield
posts.excerpt: A correct answer written in the wrong format scores zero. Dates, money, phone numbers, plurals, postcodes and spelled names — every accepted variant.
